newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Dull Australian stocks extend losses by close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Dull Australian stocks extend losses by close.

text.p: *Stocks end down, big banks lose amid fears on U.S. rates, look to Wall Street, local jobs. Volume 388.61 million, value A$748.17 million, 1,106 stocks traded, 350 steady, 333 up, 423 down.
The Australian share market closed lower on Wednesday with fears on U.S. interest rates and Dow direction giving the big banks a drubbing.
By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 13.9 points lower at 2,454.4.
The March share index futures contract was 10 points lower at 2,457, a 2.6 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said early losses were extended in the afternoon session as investors chose to move to the sidelines rather than commit funds with questions still hanging over Wall Street.
"It has been reasonably weak and there hasn't been the support in many of the stocks," said dealer Peter Struk of Reynolds and Co.
"People have been happy to let its slide and wait to see what the Dow does tonight."

Commonwealth Bank of Australia, down nearly two percent to A$12.939, and National Australia Bank, dipping 1.3 percent to A$15.85, bore the brunt in the industrials as buyers chose to stay away. Elsewhere, bellwether BHP suffered for its leading role, losing one percent to A$17.14, while the other major miners ended mixed.
Results continued with upmarket retailer David Jones posting a 50 percent lower first half net profit of A$22.34 million. Its shares lost three cents to A$1.71.

After trading closed, the company announced it had appointed Peter Wilkinson as its new chief executive officer, replacing Chris Tideman who resigned on March 10. Wilkinson is currently managing director at Just Jeans Holdings Ltd.
Delta Gold shares ended steady at A$2.12 in a generally soft market after its 45 percent jump in first half net profit to A$10.04 million.
Gold miner Resolute lost six cents to A$2.87 after a fall in first half net profit to A$15.06 million.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to seven, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options and futures trade was moderate activity-wise, but was characterised by the same lack of features afflicting the underlying markets.
